name: Ahrefs
billing_model: Subscription with a monthly pool of API units.

spend_api.returns: `units_limit_workspace`, `units_usage_workspace`, `units_limit_api_key`, `units_usage_api_key`, `usage_reset_date` and `subscription`
spend_api.read_only_note: Per-key unit caps exist. A read-only key is not documented.

native_caps.name: Per-key unit limit
native_caps.note: The API reports `units_limit_api_key`, so a key can carry its own unit cap.

name: Algolia
billing_model: Plan based. Paid plans include search requests and records, then bill overage. Free plans are blocked until the next billing cycle instead.

spend_api.returns: Time series of `t` (timestamp in ms) and `v` (value) for usage metrics such as records, search requests and operations. It returns usage counts, not dollars.
spend_api.key_type: API key from the Usage section of the API Keys page
spend_api.read_only_note: The docs name a key in the Usage section of the API Keys page but do not describe its permissions.
spend_api.notes: Requires the Premium plan or an Enterprise add-on. Needs startDate and endDate, with optional hourly (up to 7 days) or daily (up to 365 days) granularity. A per-index form is GET /1/usage/{statistic}/{index}.

name: Anthropic
billing_model: Pay as you go per token, with prepaid credits or invoicing by tier.

spend_api.returns: daily cost buckets in USD (decimal strings in cents) for the organization, grouped by workspace and description if you ask
spend_api.key_type: Admin API key, or a service account or personal key that isn't scoped to a workspace
spend_api.read_only_note: Anthropic has no read-only key for the cost report. A service account or personal key can do whatever its linked account's role allows. An Admin API key can also manage members, workspaces and API keys.
spend_api.rate_limit: Anthropic supports polling once a minute for sustained use.
spend_api.lag: Usually within 5 minutes of a request, though sometimes longer. Priority Tier costs are not included.
spend_api.notes: Workspace-scoped keys don't work. The cost report needs a Claude Console organization: an individual Console account must set up an organization first, and it isn't available on the claude.ai Team plan. Anthropic now recommends its Usage and Cost Analytics API for new integrations; this endpoint remains supported.

setup_steps.title: Use an organization, not an Individual Org
setup_steps.detail: The cost report isn't available to individual Console accounts. If the Console shows an Individual Org, set up an organization first.

setup_steps.title: Create a service account (recommended)
setup_steps.detail: An organization admin creates it on the Service accounts page. Its key acts only as that service account, with its permissions, and isn't tied to you.

setup_steps.title: Create a key that isn't scoped to a workspace
setup_steps.detail: On API keys, set Linked account to the service account (or yourself) and leave the workspace unset. Workspace keys won't work. An Admin API key (sk-ant-admin…) from Admin keys also works.

extra_faq.q: Can I use a regular Claude API key?
extra_faq.a: Only if it isn't scoped to a workspace. A service account or personal key with no workspace works, and so does an Admin API key. Workspace keys don't.

extra_faq.q: Does it work with an individual Console account?
extra_faq.a: Not as is. The cost report isn't available to individual Console accounts. Set up an organization in the Claude Console first, then create the key there.

page.title: Claude Billing API: Read Your Spend in Code | Kill Cord
page.h1: The Claude billing API: read your spend in code
page.lede: Anthropic’s cost report gives you Claude API spend over HTTP. Here’s the call, the key it needs, and the limit that stops spend on its own.

native_caps.name: Organization spend limit
native_caps.note: Past it, API requests fail until next month or until you raise it. The API cannot read this setting.

native_caps.name: Workspace spend limit
native_caps.where: Claude Console › Settings › Workspaces, then Spend limits
native_caps.note: The Default Workspace cannot have a limit, so put production keys in their own workspace.

name: Apify
billing_model: Monthly subscription with prepaid usage credits, then pay as you go for overage, billed in USD.

spend_api.returns: `monthlyUsageCycle` (startAt, endAt), `limits` (including `maxMonthlyUsageUsd`) and `current` usage (including `monthlyUsageUsd`, compute units, proxy and data transfer).
spend_api.auth: Authorization: Bearer <API token> (query parameter `token` also works but header is recommended)
spend_api.key_type: Personal or organization API token, optionally scoped with Limit token permissions
spend_api.read_only_note: Scoped tokens can be limited to chosen resources. The docs do not list a permission that covers reading limits and usage only.
spend_api.notes: A second endpoint, GET /v2/users/me/usage/monthly, returns daily usage and `totalUsageCreditsUsdAfterVolumeDiscount` for a cycle. PUT /v2/users/me/limits updates `maxMonthlyUsageUsd`. Plan price figures differ between the docs and the pricing page.

native_caps.name: Custom monthly usage limit
native_caps.where: Console › Billing › Limits › Custom usage limit (Edit)
native_caps.note: When usage passes the limit, platform services are suspended. Each plan has a ceiling on how high you can set it. Overage can be switched on or off on paid plans.

native_caps.name: Usage limit notifications
native_caps.note: Apify notifies you as you approach limits. Thresholds are not documented.

name: Apollo
billing_model: Credits per billing cycle, by credit type.

spend_api.returns: `limit`, `consumed` and `left_over` for each credit type
spend_api.read_only_note: It needs the master key, which can do everything else too.
spend_api.rate_limit: About 200 requests a minute per team on Basic and Pro, with 429 and retry-after.
spend_api.notes: On unified-credit plans, do not add the per-type balances together.

name: AssemblyAI
billing_model: Prepaid balance on pay-as-you-go accounts, topped up by auto-pay, or contracted billing.

spend_api.lag: Dashboard usage and spend update every 2 minutes. A streaming session must close before its usage appears.
spend_api.notes: Account management docs list balance, cost and usage only in the dashboard (Workspace › Manage › Cost and Usage). They mention no API for it.

native_caps.name: Auto-pay top-up
native_caps.note: Without auto-pay, a zero or negative balance restricts API access.

native_caps.name: Usage and balance alerts
native_caps.note: Owners and Admins can create them.

killcord.note: Not read live: AssemblyAI has no billing API. Kill Cord has a preset for it: add AssemblyAI as a manual entry with your plan, price and renewal date, and Kill Cord shows it as not live, keeps it out of your totals, and reminds you before it renews. Its caps audit also walks you through AssemblyAI’s own spend controls.

name: AWS
billing_model: Pay as you go per service, billed monthly.

spend_api.returns: cost and usage grouped by service, account or tag, for a date range
spend_api.key_type: IAM user or role with ce:GetCostAndUsage
spend_api.read_only_note: An IAM policy can allow only ce:Get* actions.
spend_api.lag: Data refreshes at least once every 24 hours.
spend_api.cost_to_call: $0.01 per request, and each page of results counts as a request

native_caps.name: AWS Budgets
native_caps.note: Alerts by default. Budget actions can apply IAM or SCP policies or stop some instances.

name: Microsoft Azure
billing_model: Pay as you go, billed monthly for each resource and meter you use. Azure OpenAI and other Foundry models bill through the same Cost Management data.

spend_api.returns: Cost rows in `properties.rows` with `properties.columns`, shaped by the dataset, grouping and aggregation (for example `PreTaxCost` summed by day or resource group) you send, with `nextLink` for paging
spend_api.auth: Authorization: Bearer <Microsoft Entra ID OAuth2 token>
spend_api.key_type: Entra ID token for a user or service principal (no API key)
spend_api.read_only_note: Cost Management Reader or Reader on the subscription or resource group is enough to read cost data. It cannot create resources.
spend_api.rate_limit: Per tenant: 12 query processing units per 10 seconds, 60 per minute and 600 per hour. A 429 returns a retry-after header.
spend_api.lag: Cost data refreshes every four hours. Microsoft recommends calling no more than once a day.
spend_api.notes: The scope can be a subscription, resource group, billing account, management group and more. Azure OpenAI and Foundry model cost appears here 8 to 24 hours after usage. Real-time usage is in Azure Monitor.

native_caps.name: Azure Cost Management budget
native_caps.note: Budgets send alerts and can trigger action groups, but they cannot block requests. Costs are evaluated once a day.

native_caps.name: Foundry cost controls (preview)
native_caps.where: Foundry portal › Manage › Cost › Cost Control
native_caps.note: For Foundry and Azure OpenAI models only. A policy with a budget and a reset period that can send alerts or block requests, tracked in real time. It is in preview, and totals can drift from the bill.

native_caps.name: AI gateway token limits
native_caps.note: Caps tokens for a project's model deployment. This limits tokens, not dollars.

name: Bland AI
billing_model: Prepaid credits, with optional auto refill.

spend_api.returns: `billing.current_balance` and `billing.refill_to`
spend_api.read_only_note: Every restricted key can read /v1/me; one with only Analytics read can't place calls. Restricted keys are rolling out by organization.
spend_api.notes: Bland documents the balance as a number of credits and states no credit-to-dollar rate.

native_caps.name: Prepaid credits, auto refill off
native_caps.note: Usage stops when the credits run out, though it can pass zero first.

name: Brevo
billing_model: Monthly plan with a send allowance, plus optional prepaid pay-as-you-go email credits that do not expire.

spend_api.returns: A `plan` array with remaining `credits`, `creditsType` (sendLimit), plan `type` (payAsYouGo, free, subscription, sms), `startDate` and `endDate`.
spend_api.auth: Header: api-key: <API key> (OAuth 2.0 bearer token also listed)
spend_api.key_type: Brevo v3 API key (an OAuth 2.0 machine-to-machine token is also offered)
spend_api.read_only_note: The docs list one key type and do not describe read-only keys.
spend_api.rate_limit: Not listed for this endpoint. The general table gives 100 requests per hour for endpoints not named, 200 on Professional, 600 on Enterprise.
spend_api.notes: The Free plan has a daily send limit of 300 emails. Prepaid email credits do not expire and are used after the monthly plan allowance runs out. No account spend cap is documented.

name: Bright Data
billing_model: Prepaid account balance or monthly commitment, with usage billed per GB, request, or record by product.

spend_api.returns: `balance` (available funds), `credit`, `prepayment`, and `pending_costs` (usage expected on next invoice).
spend_api.key_type: Account API key tied to a user with a permission level
spend_api.read_only_note: Permission levels are Admin, Finance (billing and financial pages only), Ops, Limit, and User. Finance looks closest to billing-only, but the docs do not say which level may call this endpoint.
spend_api.notes: Free tier credits are not in this response (use GET /trials/free_tier). No API reports auto-recharge status, so check Billing settings. Only admins can create API keys, and each user gets one key.

native_caps.name: Zone usage limit
native_caps.where: Proxies and Scraping Infrastructure › zone › Configuration › Advanced settings › Usage limit
native_caps.note: Per-zone cap in dollars or bytes, per day or per month. Action can be suspend, alert, or both. Checked every 15 minutes, so it may overshoot. Older FAQ pages describe only a daily limit.

native_caps.name: Balance alerts
native_caps.note: Usage docs say an email goes out at 85% of the monthly balance used.

name: Browserbase
billing_model: Monthly plan with included browser hours and proxy bandwidth, then pay as you go overage with no cap.

spend_api.returns: `browserMinutes` and `proxyBytes` as integers. No dollar spend, plan allowance, or remaining balance.
spend_api.notes: The docs suggest building your own alerts on this endpoint. The dashboard usage view updates in real time. Concurrency is a separate org-level limit (429 when reached). The reference page says the key is on the settings page. The plans page says included hours and bandwidth are allocations, not limits, with no caps or cut-offs, and describes no spend limit or alert settings.

name: Cartesia
billing_model: A monthly plan of credits, with optional overages.

spend_api.returns: `data[].credits`: credits used per bucket
spend_api.read_only_note: Admin keys can also manage users and invites. No credits-left field.

native_caps.name: Overages off
native_caps.note: Requests that would exceed the allotment fail until renewal.

name: Cerebras
billing_model: Prepaid credits bought in the Cloud Console, optional auto-recharge, or per-model monthly subscriptions.

spend_api.lag: Cost view may be delayed by up to 10 minutes.
spend_api.notes: Docs show balance on Billing › Overview and cost under Analytics › Cost, with CSV export, and mention no API.

native_caps.name: Auto-recharge
native_caps.where: Cloud Console › Billing › Pay as you go
native_caps.note: Off by default. You set a threshold and a top-off amount.

killcord.note: Not read live: Cerebras has no billing API. Kill Cord has a preset for it: add Cerebras as a manual entry with your plan, price and renewal date, and Kill Cord shows it as not live, keeps it out of your totals, and reminds you before it renews. Its caps audit also walks you through Cerebras’s own spend controls.

name: Cloudflare
billing_model: Plan fees plus pay-as-you-go usage for Workers, R2 and other products.

spend_api.returns: billable usage and cost for the billing period; spend policies at /billing/spend-policies
spend_api.read_only_note: A token with only Billing Read cannot change anything.
spend_api.lag: Billable usage updates once a day, so today is usually missing.
spend_api.notes: Pay-as-you-go accounts only.

native_caps.name: Spend Management limit
native_caps.note: Covers Workers and Durable Objects only. Metering delays can let spend pass it.

native_caps.name: Budget alerts
native_caps.note: Recalculated daily.

name: Cohere
billing_model: Free rate-limited trial keys, then production keys billed per token, per search for rerank.

spend_api.notes: Docs checked (pricing, FAQ, errors) describe no usage or balance API. Each chat response returns billed_units, which can be summed client-side.

native_caps.name: Monthly spending limit
native_caps.where: Dashboard > Billing & Usage > Spending Limit tab
native_caps.note: Requests return HTTP 402 once the account reaches its billing limit, and capacity resets at the start of the next month.

killcord.note: Not read live: Cohere has no billing API. Kill Cord has a preset for it: add Cohere as a manual entry with your plan, price and renewal date, and Kill Cord shows it as not live, keeps it out of your totals, and reminds you before it renews.

name: DataForSEO
billing_model: Prepaid USD deposit, charged per API call.

spend_api.returns: `money.balance` (USD left), `money.total` (deposited), `money.statistics` (spend per function by day and minute), `money.limits` and `rates`
spend_api.auth: HTTP Basic with your API login and API password
spend_api.read_only_note: The API password is the full-power credential.
spend_api.rate_limit: Platform default 2,000 calls a minute and 30 concurrent
spend_api.notes: The response also lists per-function spending limits in `money.limits`; the docs do not say whether they stop calls.

name: Deepgram
billing_model: Pay as you go with prepaid credits and optional auto-load, or contracted credits.

spend_api.returns: A `balances` list, each with `amount`, `units` (for example USD), `balance_id` and `purchase_order_id`. GET .../balances/{balance_id} returns one balance.
spend_api.key_type: Project API key (keys carry a role)
spend_api.read_only_note: Docs say keys have roles, but the role permissions and which can read balances are not stated on the pages checked.
spend_api.notes: Balance is per project. The API overview also lists project usage, usage breakdown and billing breakdown endpoints.

native_caps.name: Auto-load (auto-reload) of credits
native_caps.note: Terms say threshold and amount are configurable and it can be disabled in Billing. Turn it off so spend cannot exceed the balance.

name: DeepSeek
billing_model: Per-token charges deducted from a topped-up balance or a granted balance, granted balance first.

spend_api.returns: `is_available` (balance is enough for calls) and `balance_infos` with, per currency, `currency`, `total_balance`, `granted_balance` and `topped_up_balance` (strings).
spend_api.auth: Authorization: Bearer <API key>, as for the rest of the API
spend_api.read_only_note: No read-only key is documented. The same key runs requests.
spend_api.notes: Each balance entry is in CNY or USD. The endpoint page does not show the auth header; the rest of the API uses Bearer.

name: DigitalOcean
billing_model: Pay as you go, billed monthly in arrears per resource, with optional prepayment.

spend_api.returns: `account_balance` (last billing activity, excludes month to date), `month_to_date_usage`, `month_to_date_balance`, and `generated_at`.
spend_api.key_type: Personal access token with custom scopes
spend_api.read_only_note: A custom scope `billing:read` (View and receive billing and invoice information) lets a token read billing data only.
spend_api.rate_limit: 5,000 requests per hour and 250 per minute (default API limit), with ratelimit-* headers
spend_api.lag: `generated_at` shows when the balances were last generated. The docs give no refresh interval.
spend_api.notes: Related billing endpoints: /v2/customers/my/billing_history, /v2/customers/my/invoices, /v2/customers/my/prepayment_status, and /v2/billing/{account_urn}/insights/{start}/{end}. Scope was confirmed only for the balance endpoint.

native_caps.name: Spend alerts
native_caps.where: Control panel › Billing (see Spend Alerts doc)
native_caps.note: Emails you when monthly spend crosses percentage thresholds of a budget you set. Does not stop spend.

native_caps.name: Serverless Inference key budget (public preview)
native_caps.where: Spend alert with the pause option enabled
native_caps.note: Can pause one model access key at 100% of its budget. Applies to that key only, not the account.

name: E2B
billing_model: Usage-based billing for cloud sandboxes, shown on the console’s Usage and Billing pages.

spend_api.notes: E2B documents usage and billing in its console only (the Usage and Billing tabs). No usage or billing API is documented.

native_caps.name: Spending limit
native_caps.note: E2B says you can set spending limits on the Limits page, but its docs don’t say whether usage stops at the limit.

killcord.note: Not read live: E2B has no billing API. Kill Cord has a preset for it: add E2B as a manual entry with your plan, price and renewal date, and Kill Cord shows it as not live, keeps it out of your totals, and reminds you before it renews. Its caps audit also walks you through E2B’s own spend controls.

name: ElevenLabs
billing_model: Subscription credits each month, with usage-based overage on some plans.

spend_api.returns: `tier`, `character_count`, `character_limit` and `next_character_count_reset_unix`
spend_api.read_only_note: Keys can be limited to specific endpoints and given a credit quota.

name: Exa
billing_model: Prepaid USD credits.

spend_api.returns: `credits_usd` and `expiring_credits`
spend_api.read_only_note: Service keys can create, rotate and delete API keys. Exa enables the Team Management API per team on request.

native_caps.name: Auto recharge
native_caps.note: Buys $5 to $10,000 of credits when the balance hits a threshold. An optional monthly maximum caps these purchases. Turn it off so spend cannot exceed the balance.

native_caps.name: Per-key budget
native_caps.note: A key that reaches its budget returns 402.

name: fal
billing_model: Prepaid credits in USD.

spend_api.returns: `credits.current_balance` and `currency`
spend_api.key_type: API key with the billing:usage:read permission
spend_api.read_only_note: The endpoint page says keys on the BILLING, READONLY or FULL preset include billing:usage:read, so a billing-only key can be made.
spend_api.notes: Credit balance is also shown in the billing dashboard. Purchased credits expire 365 days after purchase.

native_caps.name: Account lock below credit threshold
native_caps.note: When the balance drops below the account's lock threshold, API requests are rejected until credits are added. Enterprise invoice-billed accounts are not locked automatically. Docs do not say where the threshold is set.

name: Firecrawl
billing_model: Plan credits each month plus pay-as-you-go credits.

spend_api.returns: `remainingCredits`, `planCredits` (plan credits only, not coupon or pay-as-you-go), `billingPeriodStart` and `billingPeriodEnd`

name: Fireworks AI
billing_model: Prepaid credits, with a monthly spend limit on total usage value.

spend_api.returns: Line items by billing category (serverless, dedicated, training) with `series` and `totalCost`. Also POST /v1/accounts/{account_id}/usageCosts:query for rated serverless cost, and GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}/billingUsage for token usage. No credit balance is documented.
spend_api.key_type: Standard API key (any key on the account)
spend_api.read_only_note: Account-scope cost queries need an account administrator. No billing-only key is documented.
spend_api.lag: Usage is bucketed daily and cached for several minutes. Rated costs can lag a day or more.
spend_api.notes: Max 31-day window per request. Embeddings and image generation are not yet in billingUsage. Docs say credit grants and purchases are reported separately but do not say where. The docs list endpoint paths only, not the host.

native_caps.name: Monthly spend limit
native_caps.where: Set with `firectl quota update monthly-spend-usd --value <AMOUNT>`, check with `firectl quota list`
native_caps.note: Counts usage paid by credits too. Adding credits does not raise it. Requests pause at 100% across serverless, deployments and training.

native_caps.name: Spend notifications
native_caps.where: Billing page (default email at 80% of the limit)
native_caps.note: Enterprise spend alerts do not pause service.

name: Fly.io
billing_model: Pay as you go per organization, billed monthly, with optional prepaid credits drawn down at period end.

spend_api.notes: Fly.io documents no billing or usage API. The docs point to the dashboard: the current month to date bill, the Upcoming Invoice and the Cost Explorer. Invoices open in a Stripe billing portal. Fly.io states it does not support billing alerts. Prepaid credits are for customers without a card and are drawn down each month.

name: Gemini API
billing_model: New accounts start on a free tier. You move to a paid tier by linking a Cloud Billing account, and you can prepay credits or be invoiced after the fact.

spend_api.notes: The Gemini API billing page points to the AI Studio Usage, Spend and Billing pages for usage and cost. It describes no API for reading spend or usage, and no other route such as a billing export is named there. Billing is set per Cloud Billing account, not per key.

native_caps.name: Project spend cap
native_caps.note: Project editors, owners and admins can set it. Google calls project caps experimental, and spend can run over the cap during about 10 minutes of billing latency.

native_caps.name: Billing account tier cap
native_caps.where: Set by your tier, not by you
native_caps.note: Tier 1 is $250 a month, Tier 2 is $2,000, and Tier 3 runs from $20,000 to $100,000 or more. Service pauses for all linked projects until the next billing cycle. It can also overrun during billing latency.

native_caps.name: Cloud Billing budget
native_caps.where: Google Cloud console › Billing › Budgets & alerts
native_caps.note: A standard budget only sends alerts. Google says it does not cap usage or spending. It can publish to Pub/Sub so you can automate a response.

name: GitHub
billing_model: Metered Actions minutes, Copilot, Codespaces and storage.

spend_api.returns: `usageItems` with `grossAmount`, `netAmount`, `quantity` and `unitType` (users: /users/{username}/settings/billing/usage)
spend_api.read_only_note: The exact fine-grained permission is not stated on the endpoint page.
spend_api.notes: Needs the enhanced billing platform.

native_caps.name: Budget with Stop usage when budget limit is reached
native_caps.where: Billing and licensing › Budgets and alerts › New budget
native_caps.note: For metered products. Without that option, a budget only sends email.

name: Gojiberry
billing_model: Subscription with seats; directory reveals cost credits.

spend_api.rate_limit: 100 a minute and 100,000 a day per account
spend_api.notes: The organization and user endpoints carry no credits, plan or usage. API keys are created in the app under Settings > API and shown once. Rate limits are shared across all of a user's API keys and MCP connections.

killcord.note: Not read live: Gojiberry's API reports the credits each call uses, but no balance. Kill Cord has a preset for it: add Gojiberry as a manual entry with your plan, price and renewal date, and Kill Cord shows it as not live, keeps it out of your totals, and reminds you before it renews.

name: Google Cloud and Gemini
billing_model: Pay as you go, billed to a Cloud Billing account. The Gemini API bills the same way once billing is on.

spend_api.endpoint: Cloud Billing export to BigQuery, read with POST https://bigquery.googleapis.com/bigquery/v2/projects/{projectId}/queries
spend_api.returns: cost rows from the standard usage cost export table, which you sum by day or month
spend_api.auth: OAuth access token from a service account (scopes bigquery.readonly and cloud-billing)
spend_api.key_type: Service account key with BigQuery Data Viewer and BigQuery Job User
spend_api.read_only_note: Grant only read roles on the export dataset. Nothing that can change resources.
spend_api.lag: Hours behind, typically up to a day, with no guarantee.
spend_api.cost_to_call: BigQuery query pricing applies to the scan
spend_api.notes: There is no direct "current spend" endpoint. You turn on the billing export once, then query it.

native_caps.name: Spend cap budget
native_caps.where: Billing › Budgets & alerts, scoped to one project and one service
native_caps.note: Google says enforcement is not instant and overages are billed.

native_caps.name: AI Studio project spend cap
native_caps.note: Google calls it experimental. It can lag about 10 minutes.

native_caps.name: Budget alerts
native_caps.note: An alerts-only budget does not cap spending.

name: Groq
billing_model: Postpaid pay as you go, invoiced monthly in arrears, with early bills at usage thresholds.

spend_api.lag: Spend is tracked with a 10 to 15 minute delay.
spend_api.notes: Groq documents usage and spend only in the console (Dashboard › Usage, Settings › Billing). No usage or billing API is documented.

native_caps.name: Monthly spend limit
native_caps.note: Blocks new calls from all keys in the org (400 blocked_api_access). Resets on the 1st. Needs paid tier and org owner.

native_caps.name: Spend alerts
native_caps.note: USD thresholds (docs suggest 50, 75 and 90 percent), emailed to billing addresses set under Settings › Billing › Manage.

killcord.note: Not read live: Groq has no billing API. Kill Cord has a preset for it: add Groq as a manual entry with your plan, price and renewal date, and Kill Cord shows it as not live, keeps it out of your totals, and reminds you before it renews. Its caps audit also walks you through Groq’s own spend controls.

name: Hugging Face
billing_model: Purchased credits plus monthly included credits (PRO, Team, Enterprise), passed through at provider rates with no markup.

spend_api.returns: Daily usage time series by member, model and provider: request counts, cost in cents, and input, output and cached input token counts.
spend_api.auth: Authorization: Bearer <HF token with permission to read the organization's billing>
spend_api.key_type: User access token with organization billing read permission
spend_api.read_only_note: Docs say to use a token with permission to read the organization's billing. Exact fine-grained permission name is not given.
spend_api.lag: Requests appear up to 2 hours after they are made.
spend_api.notes: Enterprise plan and above only, organizations only. No documented API for a personal account or for credit balance. Costs are rounded to the nearest cent per row. Limit of 31 days per page, 12 months back. Personal spend is shown on the billing page in settings.

native_caps.name: Organization spending limit
native_caps.note: Docs say admins can set a spending limit but do not describe what happens at the limit.

native_caps.name: Automatic recharge
native_caps.note: Docs recommend enabling it to avoid disruption. Turn it off so spend cannot exceed purchased credits.

name: Hunter
billing_model: Monthly credits: a search costs 1, a verification 0.5.

spend_api.returns: `plan_name`, `reset_date`, and `requests.credits` with `used` and `available` (or separate searches and verifications)
spend_api.auth: api_key query parameter, X-API-KEY header, or Bearer
spend_api.notes: When `credits` is present, searches and verifications are views of the same pool. Do not add them up. The docs example marks GET /v2/account as not charging credits.

native_caps.name: Auto-purchase monthly cap
native_caps.where: Usage page > auto purchase settings (All-in-one plans)
native_caps.note: Auto-purchase buys a credit pack when credits run out. A monthly spending cap you set pauses it once reached.

native_caps.name: 80% usage email
native_caps.note: Data Platform plans do not support credit packs or auto top-up.

name: Jina AI
billing_model: One shared token balance per API key across Reader, Search, Embeddings and Reranker. Each call spends tokens.

spend_api.notes: Jina's public docs describe how tokens are counted per product but name no endpoint for reading the remaining balance. The balance is shown in the API dashboard.

killcord.note: Not read live: Jina AI has no billing API. Kill Cord has a preset for it: add Jina AI as a manual entry with your plan, price and renewal date, and Kill Cord shows it as not live, keeps it out of your totals, and reminds you before it renews.

name: Kie.ai
billing_model: Prepaid credits that never expire (about $0.005 each).

spend_api.returns: `data` (credits left); check `code`, since failures also answer HTTP 200
spend_api.read_only_note: Keys have no scopes, but can carry usage caps and an IP allow list.

native_caps.name: Usage caps on each API key
native_caps.note: Hourly, daily and total caps per key. Kie.ai doesn't say what happens at a cap.

name: Leonardo.Ai
billing_model: Prepaid API credits, billed in dollars and separate from web app plans. Credits do not expire, and requests pause when the balance hits zero.

spend_api.read_only_note: The same key runs generations. No read-only key is documented.
spend_api.notes: Leonardo's docs describe a user information endpoint (GET /me under https://cloud.leonardo.ai/api/rest/v1) that returns subscription, prompt generation and model training token amounts. The docs reviewed do not say it returns your API credit balance, and they tell you to check the API Access page for remaining credit.

native_caps.name: Auto top-up
native_caps.note: You set a threshold and an amount, and you can view, edit or disable it at any time. With it off, spend cannot exceed your balance, and requests pause at zero.

name: LlamaCloud
billing_model: Monthly credits and plans, with pay-as-you-go usage billed on a monthly invoice.

spend_api.returns: `usage.current_invoice_total_usd_cents`, `plan.limits.max_monthly_invoice_total_usd`, `usage.active_alerts` and credit grants
spend_api.read_only_note: A key inherits its owner's privileges; project keys can't read organization usage.

native_caps.name: Monthly invoice limit
native_caps.note: Readable from the usage API, with alerts when it's exceeded.

native_caps.name: Pause jobs when credits run out
native_caps.where: Plan & Credits › When credits run out
native_caps.note: New jobs stop at zero with a 402.

name: Magister
billing_model: Monthly plan with a pool of credits (500 on Connect, 2,500 on Agent), optional overage per credit, plus separate prepaid API credits at $0.02 each.

spend_api.returns: `balance`, `held`, `available` and `price_per_credit_usd`
spend_api.read_only_note: Magister: a read-only key "can never spend credits".

native_caps.name: Overage allowance
native_caps.note: Overage is off by default, billed at $0.04 per credit. You can set an additional-credit allowance (for example 500 credits is up to $20). With overage off, metered tools pause at the limit. Leaving the allowance blank means no extra cap.

native_caps.name: API credit auto-recharge limit
native_caps.note: API credits are prepaid. Auto-recharge is optional and stops at the monthly limit you set.

native_caps.name: Per-key daily credit cap
native_caps.where: Set when an API key is created
native_caps.note: Paid calls are refused once the key reaches its cap. Resets at 00:00 UTC. Applies to that key only.

name: Mailgun
billing_model: Monthly plan with an included message volume, then per-message overage.

spend_api.returns: Filtered usage metrics for the account (the docs page does not list the response fields). GET /v5/accounts/limit/custom/monthly returns the custom monthly sending limit you set. No plan balance or spend endpoint is documented.
spend_api.auth: HTTP Basic, username `api`, password is the API key
spend_api.key_type: Account API key, optionally with an RBAC role (Admin, Developer, Support, Analyst)
spend_api.read_only_note: The Analyst role is read only for data and metrics. There is no billing-specific role.
spend_api.notes: EU accounts use https://api.eu.mailgun.net. The older GET /v3/stats/total is deprecated in favor of the Metrics API. The docs don't list the usage endpoint's response fields.

native_caps.name: Custom message limit (monthly)
native_caps.where: Profile › Manage Account › Custom Message Limit (Edit)
native_caps.note: Disables sending when the count is reached, resets monthly. Owner gets alerts at 50% and 75%, admins when disabled. Also settable via PUT /v5/accounts/limit/custom/monthly.

name: Mistral AI
billing_model: Prepaid credits with pay-as-you-go use after the included monthly usage, with optional auto recharge.

spend_api.returns: `limits.completion.total_usage`, `usage_limit`, `monthly_limit_reached` and `currency`
spend_api.read_only_note: The Admin API is a beta on Enterprise plans only. An Admin key can manage users, keys and the spending limit.

native_caps.name: Organization monthly spending limit
native_caps.note: Docs say API access can be suspended until next month or an admin raises the limit.

native_caps.name: Workspace monthly spending limit
native_caps.where: Admin Panel › Administration › Workspaces › select workspace › Settings › Monthly spending limit
native_caps.note: Cannot exceed the organization limit. Docs do not say what happens when it is reached.

native_caps.name: Auto Recharge
native_caps.where: Admin Panel › Subscriptions › Billing › Credits › Auto Recharge

name: Modal
billing_model: Usage-based compute billing, with monthly credits on some plans.

spend_api.notes: Modal reports billing through its CLI (`modal billing`) and Python SDK only, not an HTTP API.

native_caps.name: Workspace budget
native_caps.note: A monthly cap on total usage before credits.

native_caps.name: Spend limit
native_caps.note: Stops workloads that would incur more out-of-pocket charges.

killcord.note: Not read live: Modal has no billing API, only its CLI and SDK. Kill Cord has a preset for it: add Modal as a manual entry with your plan, price and renewal date, and Kill Cord shows it as not live, keeps it out of your totals, and reminds you before it renews. Its caps audit also walks you through Modal's budget and spend limit.

name: Monid
billing_model: Prepaid USD wallet.

spend_api.returns: `balance.value` (USD) and `balance.currency`; /v1/runs gives cost per run
spend_api.read_only_note: Keys carry permissions, but a read-only preset is not documented.
spend_api.notes: The endpoint comes from the official CLI source, not a docs page, so it may change.

name: Moonshot AI
billing_model: Prepaid. You recharge your balance first (minimum $1) and usage draws it down. Recharging $5 in total earns a $5 voucher.

spend_api.returns: `available_balance`: milli-cents with an Admin key, dollars with an API key
spend_api.key_type: Admin key with the billing:read scope, or an API key
spend_api.read_only_note: Admin keys carry the scopes chosen when they're made and can't call inference. Admin keys are a beta for verified organizations.

native_caps.name: Daily and monthly project budgets
native_caps.where: Project Settings › Project Budget/Rate Limit Settings
native_caps.note: When a project's spending reaches a budget, its API requests are rejected. Enforcement can lag.

name: Neon
billing_model: Plan fee plus usage for compute, storage and transfer.

spend_api.returns: consumption in usage units (compute hours, storage, transfer), not dollars; the spending limit is at /organizations/{org_id}/billing/spending_limit
spend_api.read_only_note: Neon has no read-only API key. An organization key can manage every project.
spend_api.notes: Launch, Scale and Agent plans only.

native_caps.name: Spending threshold
native_caps.note: Sends email at 80% and 100%. Projects keep running.

native_caps.name: Project consumption quotas
native_caps.note: Quotas are in usage units, not dollars. Past them, computes suspend until the next period.

name: Netlify
billing_model: Credit-based plans: a monthly credit allowance, with optional auto recharge when credits run out.

spend_api.key_type: Personal access token or OAuth2 token
spend_api.read_only_note: The API guide does not document OAuth scopes.
spend_api.rate_limit: 500 requests per minute for most calls (general API limit)
spend_api.notes: Netlify documents credit balance and usage only in the team dashboard (Usage & billing, Credit balance and Credit usage breakdown). The OpenAPI reference lists no credit or billing endpoint. GET /accounts/{account_id} returns `capabilities` with included and used counts for sites and collaborators, which is not spend.

native_caps.name: Auto recharge toggle
native_caps.where: Team settings › Billing (Team Owner only), see Configure auto-recharge
native_caps.note: Off by default. Applies to the whole team. With it off, projects pause at zero credits. Not available on Free. Personal: 500 credits for $5. Pro: 1,500 credits for $10.

native_caps.name: AI credit usage limit
native_caps.where: Team settings › AI features, see Managing AI features
native_caps.note: Stops new agent runs and active runs when reached. Covers AI inference only.

native_caps.name: Usage emails and notifications
native_caps.note: Email and in-app notice at 50%, 75% and 100% of the monthly credit allotment. Pro plans can also get notices in Slack.

name: OpenAI
billing_model: Prepaid credits or monthly invoicing, charged per token and per tool call.

spend_api.returns: daily cost buckets in USD, groupable by project and line item; the spend limit is at /v1/organization/spend_limit
spend_api.read_only_note: Admin keys work across the organization. Choose read-only if it is offered when you create one.
spend_api.lag: Not documented. Expect today to trail what you have used.

native_caps.name: Organization hard limit
native_caps.where: Settings › Organization › Limits, with Enforce a hard limit checked
native_caps.note: OpenAI says enforcement is not instantaneous, so spend can slightly exceed it.

name: OpenRouter
billing_model: Prepaid credits in USD, spent per request.

spend_api.returns: `limit`, `limit_remaining`, `usage`, and daily, weekly and monthly usage for the key. The account total is at /api/v1/credits (`total_credits`, `total_usage`) with a management key.
spend_api.key_type: Inference API key (per key) or management key (account total)
spend_api.read_only_note: A normal key reads its own limits but can also spend.
spend_api.rate_limit: Per-IP burst limit with no rate-limit headers. Back off on errors.
spend_api.lag: A short settlement window for recent requests. Usage windows reset at UTC midnight.

native_caps.name: Per-key credit limit
native_caps.where: Settings › API Keys, edit a key
native_caps.note: The `limit` on a key caps what that key can spend.

name: Perplexity API
billing_model: Prepaid API credits spent per token, per request, or per search depending on the API; keys are blocked when credits run out.

spend_api.notes: No balance or usage API is documented. The console Billing page shows balance, a usage chart and spend by key.

native_caps.name: Automatic Top Up (toggle)
native_caps.where: API Console › Buy more credits › Automatic Top Up
native_caps.note: Help center says it tops up when the balance falls below $2. Developer docs do not state a fixed figure. With it off, spend cannot exceed the loaded balance and keys are blocked at zero.

killcord.note: Not read live: Perplexity API has no billing API. Kill Cord has a preset for it: add Perplexity API as a manual entry with your plan, price and renewal date, and Kill Cord shows it as not live, keeps it out of your totals, and reminds you before it renews. Its caps audit also walks you through Perplexity API’s own spend controls.

name: Pinecone
billing_model: Usage based on read units, write units, storage and egress, with a monthly minimum by plan ($0 Starter, $20 Builder, $50 Standard, $500 Enterprise).

spend_api.returns: An asynchronous export job whose `download_url` gives a zip of FOCUS v1.4 CSV cost files, with `status`, `data_available_through` and `row_count`
spend_api.key_type: Admin API service account access token
spend_api.read_only_note: The caller needs the OrgOwner or OrgBillingAdmin role.
spend_api.rate_limit: 5 exports per hour per organization, one running at a time
spend_api.notes: Enterprise plans only. It is an export you create, poll and download, not a live balance call. The download link is valid for one hour and the file is kept for two days. Query, fetch and list responses also carry per-request read unit usage.

native_caps.name: Builder plan usage block
native_caps.where: Applies automatically on the Builder plan
native_caps.note: On Builder, usage beyond plan limits is blocked rather than billed. Starter and Builder also block reads past the egress allowance.

killcord.note: Not read live: Pinecone exports cost only as an Enterprise CSV report. Kill Cord has a preset for it: add Pinecone as a manual entry with your plan, price and renewal date, and Kill Cord shows it as not live, keeps it out of your totals, and reminds you before it renews. Its caps audit also walks you through Pinecone's spend alerts.

name: PostHog
billing_model: Usage-based, with a free monthly allowance per product.

spend_api.returns: a billing overview; /api/billing/usage/ gives a time series
spend_api.key_type: Personal API key with the billing:read scope
spend_api.read_only_note: The billing:read scope can read billing only.
spend_api.notes: The organization billing API is in beta behind a feature flag (403 without it), so shapes may change.

native_caps.name: Billing limits per product
native_caps.note: Past a limit, PostHog stops ingesting that product, and data past the limit is lost.

name: Postmark
billing_model: Monthly plan with overage billed in arrears.

spend_api.returns: a count of sent emails; remaining has to be worked out from your plan size
spend_api.key_type: Server token (account-level endpoints use a separate Account token)
spend_api.notes: There is no billing endpoint. Server tokens are on the API Tokens tab of each server. Postmark keeps sending past your plan size and bills overage in arrears. It offers no setting to turn overage off or cap it. The free Developer plan is a hard limit of 100 emails a month.

name: Railway
billing_model: Subscription plan plus usage-based compute and other resources, billed per cycle.

spend_api.returns: Usage by project for a billing period (memory, CPU, network egress, disk and backup measurements), estimated usage for the current period, the workspace usage limit (`softLimit`, `hardLimit`, `isOverLimit`), and agent usage in cents (`totalUsedCents`, `hardLimitCents`, `usageRemaining`). Dollar totals for compute are not returned; the CLI works them out from fixed rates.
spend_api.key_type: Account, workspace, project, or OAuth token
spend_api.rate_limit: Per hour: 100 Free, 1,000 Hobby, 10,000 Pro. Per second: 10 Hobby, 50 Pro. HTTP 429 with Retry-After.
spend_api.notes: The official CLI’s `railway usage` command reads these through the GraphQL API. The Public API docs do not document usage or cost queries. The official CLI source uses them, so they can change without notice. The `railway usage`, `railway usage projects` and `railway usage limit status` commands wrap them. Account and workspace tokens are created at the key URL, project tokens in project settings.

native_caps.name: Hard usage limit
native_caps.where: Workspace Usage page (railway.com/workspace/usage) › Set Usage Limits › Hard limit
native_caps.note: Max spend per billing cycle, set separately for Compute and Agent usage. Minimum $10. Workloads go offline at the limit. Reminders at 75%, 90%, 100%. Also settable with `railway usage limit set`. Agent limit cannot be removed.

native_caps.name: Custom email alert
native_caps.where: Workspace Usage page › Set Usage Limits › Custom email alert
native_caps.note: Soft limit that emails you. Resources keep running.

name: Render
billing_model: Workspace plan plus per-instance monthly charges, with usage-based bandwidth and build pipeline minutes.

spend_api.key_type: Render API key tied to one workspace, with per-resource permissions
spend_api.read_only_note: A key can be set to read-only access across resources. The docs list no billing permission and no billing endpoint.
spend_api.rate_limit: Most GET endpoints: 400 requests per minute, per user
spend_api.notes: The API reference has no billing, invoice or spend endpoints. It does have Metrics endpoints for bandwidth, CPU, memory and disk usage. Accrued charges are shown on the dashboard Billing page.

native_caps.name: Build pipeline spend limit
native_caps.where: Workspace Settings › Build Pipeline › Set spend limit
native_caps.note: Stops auto-buying extra pipeline minutes once reached. Covers pipeline minutes only, not the whole bill.

name: Replicate
billing_model: Pay as you go for compute time, either prepaid credit or postpaid billed monthly in arrears.

spend_api.notes: The billing docs point only to the account billing page. No billing API is documented.

native_caps.name: Prepaid credit at zero
native_caps.note: On prepaid credit, when the balance hits zero Replicate stops new work from starting and shuts down what it’s running for you. Auto reload tops it up if it’s on. The monthly spend limit was retired in 2025; accounts billed in arrears have no cap.

killcord.note: Not read live: Replicate has no billing API. Kill Cord has a preset for it: add Replicate as a manual entry with your plan, price and renewal date, and Kill Cord shows it as not live, keeps it out of your totals, and reminds you before it renews. Its caps audit also walks you through Replicate’s own spend controls.

name: Resend
billing_model: Subscription with a monthly email quota, plus pay-as-you-go.

spend_api.returns: `x-resend-monthly-quota` and, on the free plan, `x-resend-daily-quota`: emails used
spend_api.read_only_note: A Sending access key can't make any read, so this needs a Full access key, which can manage domains and keys.

native_caps.name: Overages off, or an overage limit
native_caps.note: With overages off, sending stops at the monthly quota. With them on, sending pauses at the overage limit (400% by default).

name: Retell AI
billing_model: Prepaid credits, with an optional monthly budget and auto recharge.

spend_api.returns: Calls with `call_cost.combined_cost` (cents), added up by Kill Cord
spend_api.key_type: API key limited to History › Read
spend_api.read_only_note: Keys can be restricted; History › Read reads call history but can't place calls. No balance or spend endpoint.

native_caps.name: Monthly budget
native_caps.note: At 100%, calls and API requests pause until the next month.

native_caps.name: Auto recharge off
native_caps.note: Usage stops at $0 until you buy credits.

name: Runway
billing_model: Prepaid credits. You buy credits ($10 per 1,000) and each generation spends them. Autobilling can top up when the balance runs low.

spend_api.returns: `creditBalance` (credits remaining), `tier` (including `maxMonthlyCreditSpend` and per-model daily and concurrent generation limits) and `usage` (daily generations per model)
spend_api.read_only_note: The same key runs generations. No read-only key is documented.
spend_api.notes: A separate POST /v1/organization/usage endpoint returns credit usage by model for a time range.

native_caps.name: Tier monthly spend limit
native_caps.where: Set by your usage tier (rises as you buy credits)
native_caps.note: Tiers cap monthly credit purchases at $100, $500, $2,000, $20,000 or $100,000. Once you hit it you cannot buy more credits, and autobilling is capped at what remains.

native_caps.name: Autobilling threshold
native_caps.note: Checks hourly and recharges when the balance drops below your threshold, with a minimum recharge of $10. Runway's docs do not say how to turn it off.

name: ScrapeCreators
billing_model: Prepaid credits that never expire.

spend_api.returns: `creditCount` (credits left) and a `message`
spend_api.rate_limit: Scrape Creators enforces no API rate limits. The docs recommend staying under 500 concurrent requests.
spend_api.notes: The docs say checking your balance is free and does not deduct credits. A 402 response means you need to buy more credits. The docs describe no auto top-up or spend cap.

name: ScraperAPI
billing_model: Monthly subscription with a pool of API credits, where premium and rendering options cost more credits.

spend_api.returns: Request usage counts, named in the docs as `requestCount`, `failedRequestCount`, and `concurrentRequests`. The docs page does not list a plan limit or credits remaining field.
spend_api.read_only_note: The same key runs scrape requests. No separate read-only key is documented.
spend_api.lag: `requestCount` and `failedRequestCount` refresh about every 15 seconds. `concurrentRequests` is real time.
spend_api.notes: Full response fields are not documented on the page fetched. A separate GET /account/urlcost returns the credit cost of a URL. Keys can be regenerated once every 24 hours.

native_caps.name: max_cost parameter
native_caps.where: Request parameter, not a console setting
native_caps.note: Caps credits per request. A request that would exceed it returns 403. Not an account-wide cap.

name: Scrapfly
billing_model: A monthly plan of API credits, with optional pay-as-you-go extra use.

spend_api.returns: `subscription.usage.scrape` (`current`, `limit`, `remaining`) and `subscription.period`
spend_api.read_only_note: One key per project environment, with access to every product.

native_caps.name: No extra credit use on each project
native_caps.note: With Allow PAG off, calls past the quota are refused instead of billed. Or keep it and set a Budget Limit.

name: ScrapingBee
billing_model: Monthly subscription with a pool of API credits, where features cost different credits per request.

spend_api.returns: `max_api_credit`, `used_api_credit`, `max_concurrency`, `current_concurrency`, and `renewal_subscription_date`.
spend_api.read_only_note: The same key runs scrape requests. No separate read-only key is documented.
spend_api.notes: Calls to it don't count toward concurrency. The docs don't say whether the call uses credits.

native_caps.name: max_cost parameter (Auto-Mode)
native_caps.where: Request parameter, not a console setting
native_caps.note: Caps the credits a single Auto-Mode request may spend. It is per request only, not an account cap.

name: ScreenshotOne
billing_model: Monthly request quota.

spend_api.returns: `total`, `available`, `used`, and `concurrency` with `limit`, `remaining` and `reset`
spend_api.rate_limit: `concurrency` shows the per-minute request bucket for your plan (`limit`, `remaining`, `reset`).
spend_api.notes: Only successful requests count toward `used`. `concurrency` values are request-bucket values, not active render counts.

native_caps.name: Overage off by default
native_caps.where: Dashboard (overage and monthly hard limit settings, paid plans)
native_caps.note: With overage off, requests past the plan quota fail with a limit error. With overage on, you set a monthly hard limit, up to a plan maximum.

native_caps.name: Quota emails
native_caps.note: Emails at 90% and 100% of the monthly quota.

name: Semrush
billing_model: Subscription plus a pool of API units.

spend_api.returns: a plain number: your remaining API units

name: Twilio SendGrid
billing_model: Monthly plan with a base email allowance, then per-email overage charges.

spend_api.returns: Credits as `remain`, `total`, `used`, `overage`, plus `last_reset`, `next_reset`, and `reset_frequency`.
spend_api.key_type: SendGrid API key (Full Access, Custom Access, or Billing Access)
spend_api.read_only_note: A Billing Access key type exists for the billing endpoints. The docs do not say whether it covers /v3/user/credits.
spend_api.notes: EU regional subusers use https://api.eu.sendgrid.com. A parent account can read a subuser with the on-behalf-of header.

native_caps.name: Usage limit alert
native_caps.note: Emails you when a set share of your plan's emails is used. New accounts get a 90% alert by default. It does not stop sending.

name: SerpApi
billing_model: Monthly plan with a set number of searches per month, plus optional extra credits.

spend_api.returns: `plan_searches_left`, `total_searches_left`, `extra_credits`, `searches_per_month`, `this_month_usage`, `this_hour_searches`, `last_hour_searches`, `account_rate_limit_per_hour`, `plan_name`, `plan_monthly_price`, and `plan_renewal_date`.
spend_api.read_only_note: The same private key runs searches. No separate read-only key is documented.
spend_api.notes: Docs say the Account API is free and does not count toward the monthly quota. The response also echoes the API key. `account_rate_limit_per_hour` is the plan's hourly search throughput.

native_caps.name: Monthly search quota
native_caps.note: At the plan's monthly cap the API returns HTTP 429 until renewal or upgrade. Enterprise plans can bill beyond the reserved amount.

name: Snov.io
billing_model: Monthly credits.

spend_api.returns: `balance` (credits), `teamwork`, `unique_recipients_used` and `limit_resets_in`
spend_api.auth: Bearer token from POST /v1/oauth/access_token with your User ID and Secret (expires after 1 hour)
spend_api.key_type: API client ID and client secret
spend_api.notes: Access token expires after 3600 seconds. Credits refresh each 30-day billing period.

name: Stability AI
billing_model: Prepaid credits, each successful request consumes credits (1 credit is $0.01).

spend_api.returns: `credits`, the balance of the account or organization tied to the key.
spend_api.read_only_note: No read-only key is documented. The same key generates images.
spend_api.notes: Optional Organization header scopes the call to another organization. Pricing page says 1 credit equals $0.01.

name: Supabase
billing_model: Plan fee plus usage-based charges past each plan quota.

spend_api.notes: The Management API has no billing or usage endpoint. The Upcoming Invoice is on the Billing page.

native_caps.name: Spend Cap
native_caps.note: Compute, custom domains, IPv4, PITR and some other items bill even with the cap on.

name: Tavily
billing_model: Credit based. A monthly plan includes credits, and optional pay as you go bills $0.008 per credit once the plan's credits run out.

spend_api.returns: `key` object with `usage`, `search_usage`, `extract_usage`, `crawl_usage`, `map_usage`, `research_usage` and `limit`, and an `account` object with `current_plan`, `plan_usage`, `plan_limit`, `paygo_usage` and `paygo_limit`
spend_api.read_only_note: The same key runs searches. No read-only key is documented.
spend_api.notes: Usage is for the current billing cycle. `limit` is the key's own usage limit and is null when the key is unlimited. An optional X-Project-ID header scopes the query to one project. Pricing figures come from the docs and can change.

name: Together AI
billing_model: Prepaid credits that must stay above zero, with optional auto-recharge.

spend_api.returns: Daily windows of line items with `cost` (USD, decimal strings)
spend_api.read_only_note: Any project's key reads the whole organization's report. The endpoint is a beta Together enables per organization; others get 404.

native_caps.name: Balance cut-off at zero
native_caps.note: Metering has a short delay, so it is not an exact cap.

native_caps.name: Auto-recharge
native_caps.note: Docs state auto-recharge does not cap spend. Turn it off so spend cannot exceed the balance.

name: treg
billing_model: Prepaid USD balance, held in micro-USD.

spend_api.returns: `balance_micro`, `balance_usd`, and `holds` (in-flight reservations); /usage/me gives `spent_today_micro` and `daily_spend_cap_micro`
spend_api.auth: X-Treg-Token: <token> (a personal token also needs X-Treg-Org)
spend_api.read_only_note: Any member, including the viewer role, can read the balance. A key that can never spend is not documented.
spend_api.notes: The route comes from the official tools-registry package source; the public docs document the CLI and MCP balance tool.

name: Truelist
billing_model: Credits, 100 to start. A credit is used only when an address has not been verified in the last 30 days.

spend_api.returns: account name, plan and settings; no credit count is documented

killcord.note: Not read live: Truelist's API reports your plan's name but no credit balance. Kill Cord has a preset for it: add Truelist as a manual entry with your plan, price and renewal date, and Kill Cord shows it as not live, keeps it out of your totals, and reminds you before it renews.

name: Twelve Labs
billing_model: Plans with allowances; past an allowance, requests fail unless overage is on.

spend_api.notes: Twelve Labs shows plans and usage in the Playground under Settings › Billing & Plans. No usage or billing API is documented.

native_caps.name: Overage off
native_caps.note: With overage off, requests fail with an error at the allowance. Overage is off by default on Pro and on by default on Enterprise.

killcord.note: Not read live: Twelve Labs has no billing API. Kill Cord has a preset for it: add Twelve Labs as a manual entry with your plan, price and renewal date, and Kill Cord shows it as not live, keeps it out of your totals, and reminds you before it renews. Its caps audit also walks you through Twelve Labs’s own spend controls.

name: Twilio
billing_model: Prepaid balance or invoicing, charged per message, call minute and verification.

spend_api.returns: usage records with price in your account currency; Today.json gives today
spend_api.auth: HTTP Basic with an API key SID and secret (or Account SID and Auth Token)
spend_api.read_only_note: Twilio has no read-only key. A Standard API key can also send messages and make calls.
spend_api.lag: Usage records trail real usage a little.

native_caps.name: Usage trigger on total spend
native_caps.where: Console › Billing and Usage › Usage and Spend › Usage Triggers
native_caps.note: Twilio has no native hard spend cap. A trigger calls a webhook; it stops nothing on its own.

name: TypeSafe Jev
billing_model: Per input token ($0.042 per million); output tokens are currently free.

spend_api.notes: TypeSafe’s API documents only POST /v1/systemone and GET /v1/models. Responses carry usage.input_tokens and usage.output_tokens; no balance, usage or billing endpoint is documented.

killcord.note: Not read live: TypeSafe Jev has no billing API. Kill Cord has a preset for it: add TypeSafe Jev as a manual entry with your plan, price and renewal date, and Kill Cord shows it as not live, keeps it out of your totals, and reminds you before it renews.

name: Unstructured
billing_model: A prepaid balance in dollars (at least $50 at a time) that each job draws on; it expires 12 months after your last payment.

spend_api.notes: Unstructured shows the prepaid balance on its Billing page. No balance or billing API is documented; a job that the balance can’t cover fails with HTTP 402 insufficient_balance.

native_caps.name: Prepaid balance
native_caps.note: Each job’s estimated cost is reserved first; if the balance can’t cover it, the request fails before a job starts. There’s no auto top-up.

killcord.note: Not read live: Unstructured has no billing API. Kill Cord has a preset for it: add Unstructured as a manual entry with your plan, price and renewal date, and Kill Cord shows it as not live, keeps it out of your totals, and reminds you before it renews. Its caps audit also walks you through Unstructured’s own spend controls.

name: Upstash
billing_model: Pay as you go per command, storage and bandwidth, or a flat monthly fixed plan.

spend_api.returns: For one Redis database: `total_monthly_billing` (cost this month), `total_monthly_requests`, `total_monthly_read_requests`, `total_monthly_write_requests`, `total_monthly_bandwidth` (bytes) and `total_monthly_storage` (bytes), plus daily series including `dailybilling`.
spend_api.auth: HTTP Basic: account email as username, Developer API key as password
spend_api.key_type: Developer API key, Read/Write or Read Only
spend_api.read_only_note: Developer API keys can be created as Read Only or Read/Write. The docs do not say which endpoints a read-only key may call.
spend_api.notes: Stats are per database, so an account total means calling this for each database. The 30 day period option needs a Pro plan or the Production Pack. Keys are created in the console under Account, Developer API.

native_caps.name: Monthly budget per database
native_caps.where: Pay as you go database settings in the Upstash console
native_caps.note: When the budget is reached the database is rate limited instead of billing further. Budgets are per database, with no account-wide budget. Fixed plans have no budget setting.

name: Vapi
billing_model: Prepaid credits, with optional auto-reload.

spend_api.returns: A `sum` of call `cost` (USD) by day
spend_api.read_only_note: A private key can access everything in the organization. Counts call costs only.

native_caps.name: Prepaid credits, auto-reload off
native_caps.note: At $0 with auto-reload off, Vapi freezes the subscription.

name: Vercel
billing_model: Plan fee plus usage-based charges on Pro and Enterprise.

spend_api.returns: billing charges in the FOCUS format, by day and service, in USD
spend_api.auth: Authorization: Bearer <access token>, with teamId for a team
spend_api.read_only_note: Tokens have the same access as your account on the teams they are scoped to.
spend_api.lag: Reported by day. Today may be missing until tomorrow.

native_caps.name: Spend Management: pause production
native_caps.note: Pauses production deployments. It does not stop AI Gateway, v0, or storage charges.

native_caps.name: Spend Management notifications
native_caps.note: At 50%, 75% and 100% of the budget.

name: Voyage AI
billing_model: Pay as you go per token (per pixel for multimodal) after free tokens, billed through a MongoDB Atlas organization.

spend_api.key_type: Model API key created in MongoDB Atlas
spend_api.read_only_note: Viewing billing needs the Organization Billing Viewer role or higher in Atlas, which is a user role, not an API key.
spend_api.lag: Cost Explorer updates every 24 hours. The Usage page tracks tokens in real time.
spend_api.notes: Docs show usage and billing in the Atlas UI with CSV export and mention no API. Atlas has its own separate billing tooling.

killcord.note: Not read live: Voyage AI has no billing API. Kill Cord has a preset for it: add Voyage AI as a manual entry with your plan, price and renewal date, and Kill Cord shows it as not live, keeps it out of your totals, and reminds you before it renews.

name: xAI (Grok API)
billing_model: Prepaid credits first, with optional monthly invoiced billing up to an invoiced limit (default $0).

spend_api.returns: `total.val` (prepaid balance) and a `changes` list with `changeOrigin` (PURCHASE, SPEND, REFUND, MANUAL, AUTO_PURCHASE), `amount.val` and `createTime`. POST .../usage returns historical spend, tokens and units. GET .../postpaid/invoice/preview and .../postpaid/spending-limits also exist.
spend_api.key_type: Management key (separate from inference API keys)
spend_api.read_only_note: Docs say creating a management key needs the Management Keys Read + Write permission. They do not say whether a key can be limited to read.
spend_api.notes: Amounts come back as USD cents in strings. Management keys are separate from the keys that run requests.

native_caps.name: Invoiced billing limit (default $0)
native_caps.note: At $0, requests are rejected once prepaid credits run out. Raising it needs sales.

native_caps.name: Auto top-up with monthly maximum
native_caps.note: Set a balance threshold, top-up amount (min $5) and a monthly maximum for top-ups. A warning appears at 80% of the monthly limit.
